Subject: Residency, logs and retention — follow-up from discovery call (HealthLytics)

Hi Olivia — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our side: 

- Summary of ask: HealthLytics wants to process patient-identifiable inputs in the US region, ensure audit logs are available for 12 months for a subset of flows, and confirm cross-region failover behavior for DR.
- Immediate clarifications we promised to provide: retention windows for request/response logs (default vs. extended), whether logs contain raw PII, options for masking/pseudonymization, and how region pinning interacts with failover.

Action items we committed to:
1) Provide a short matrix outlining default vs. configurable retention windows and associated pricing impact (Monica)
2) Share SOC2 snapshot and a sample data handling diagram (Ben) — attached: redwood_SOC2_snapshot.pdf and a draft data_retention_matrix.xlsx
3) Confirm technical failover behavior when a pin exists (Marissa)

Timelines: Monica will reply with the retention/pricing matrix by EOD tomorrow; Marissa will give a short note on failover/pin semantics. After that, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up to review SLAs and pricing.

Anything I missed? Happy to adjust.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Residency, logs and retention — follow-up from discovery call (HealthLytics)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side to help you tailor the matrix: 

- Which logs contain full request/response payloads vs. metadata only? Our security team needs to know whether PHI could appear in logs by default.
- We require the ability to pin workloads to a US region (explicitly US-East) but also need a clear description of what happens during regional outages: is traffic routed to an EU standby, or will requests be queued/fail?
- Retention: we need 12 months for request metadata and 6 months for full request/response (where allowed). Is that achievable without a dedicated private deployment?
- Can you confirm whether KMS keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own) and whether logs are encrypted with the same key scope?

Also, can you include an audit sample or schema for the event logs so our SIEM team can map fields? If you can provide the SOC2 doc and a high-level diagram (PII flow + which stores hold raw payloads), that would be very helpful.

Appreciate it,
Olivia
Director of Product, HealthLytics
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@healthlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-02T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency, logs and retention — follow-up from discovery call (HealthLytics)

Hi Olivia — thanks, good questions. Summary below — I focused on the specific items you called out. See attached matrix (data_retention_matrix.xlsx) and a simple pseudonymization flow (pseudonymization_flow.png). I've kept answers concise; happy to expand in the follow-up call.

1) Log contents and PII exposure:
- By default, Redwood stores request metadata (timestamps, model id, token counts, route id, request id) and an encrypted copy of request/response payloads for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. That encrypted copy can contain PII if present in the prompt.
- We offer a configurable 'payload retention' toggle per route:
  * Off (default for self-serve): payloads are not stored beyond a transient 72-hour buffer used for immediate retries and observability.
  * Metadata-only: store metadata only (no payloads) — good for strict PHI use cases.
  * Payload-allowed: store encrypted payloads for X days (configurable).

2) Pseudonymization and masking options:
- We provide server-side pseudonymization hooks that can hash or redact specified JSON fields before logs hit durable storage. Customers can also use client-side transformations (recommended for maximum control).
- We included a sample pseudonymization flow (pseudonymization_flow.png).

3) Retention windows and pricing impact:
- Default: metadata 30 days, payloads (if enabled) 30 days.
- Configurable tiers we offer: 30, 90, 180, 365 days for payloads. Metadata-only retention up to 365 days is available on hosted with minimal cost delta.
- Retaining encrypted payloads for 365 days has a predictable storage cost; I put ballpark line items in the attached XLSX. If HealthLytics needs extended retention for payloads at 365 days and wants to avoid payload storage on hosted, we can discuss Dedicated or Private options (Private = customer-managed storage and KMS).

4) Region pinning and cross-region failover behavior:
- Pinning is route-level and can be locked to a specific region (e.g., us-east-1). When pinned, traffic is routed to pinned region under normal operation.
- Failover behavior (two modes):
  * Strict pin + no-failover: requests will fail if the pinned region cannot accept traffic (recommended for regulatory/sovereignty scenarios where cross-border processing is disallowed).
  * Pin-with-fallback: requests are routed to configured fallback region (e.g., us-west or eu-west) during outage. We surface this in the config and it is visible in the Console/SDK.
- Snapshots/backups: persistent storage (for payloads you have chosen to retain) is replicated to a geographically nearby backup region for durability, but replication is scope-controlled per customer. For strict residency, we can disable cross-region replication and maintain cold backups in a customer-controlled archive in the same territory (requires Private/Dedicated option).

5) KMS and encryption scope:
- Hosted: we encrypt at rest using Redwood-managed keys by default. Customers can request Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) via our KMS integrations (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) on Dedicated and Private plans; limited CMK support on Hosted for enterprise accounts (requires contract and onboarding).
- Audit logs and metadata are encrypted with keys scoped to the same tenant; payload encryption follows the same key scope if payload storage is enabled.

6) Audit schema and SIEM mapping:
- Attached is a sample audit event schema in the XLSX under the "audit_schema" tab. Event fields include request_id, user_id (if provided by the customer), route_id, model_version, start_ts, end_ts, token_count, http_status, and storage_flags.

Next steps:
- If you confirm desired retention (metadata vs. payload and duration), I will produce a short quote for incremental storage costs and any Dedicated/Private work required.
- Ben: can you capture pricing delta and draft an SOW outline if they want Private?

Thanks — I can hop on a call with your security team if helpful.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: data_retention_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, stub), pseudonymization_flow.png (PNG, stub)

Subject: Re: Residency, logs and retention — follow-up from discovery call (HealthLytics)

Olivia — quick follow-up on two items Monica raised so we can size the recommendation: 

1) If you opt for metadata-only retention for 365 days (no payloads retained), we can keep you on Hosted with no capacity changes; pricing impact is marginal (metadata ingest + storage). I'll attach a short line item in the quote.
2) If you want payload retention (365 days) and strict in-territory backups (no cross-region replication), that likely requires Dedicated or Private depending on throughput. Preliminary guidance: for your expected steady-state QPS (~12 rps peak) and retention at 365 days, estimate: Dedicated small pool (1-2 GPUs reserved) + storage provisioning. Monica, please confirm if that sizing aligns.

Can I schedule a 30-minute call Friday to walk through the quote and the pin/failover modes with your security lead? Proposed times: Fri 9/3 09:00-09:30 PT or 11:00-11:30 PT.

Ben
From: Olivia Barnes <obarnes@healthlytics.com>

Cc: HealthLytics Security <security@healthlytics.com>
Date: 2027-09-03T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency, logs and retention — follow-up from discovery call (HealthLytics)

Thanks, team — this is helpful and addresses most of our questions. We want to: 

- Move forward with metadata-only retention for 365 days on Hosted as a baseline (please send formal quote)
- Evaluate payload retention for a narrow set of routes (6 months initially) — include pricing options for 180 vs. 365 days
- For residency: we will request strict pin to us-east and no-failover for PHI routes; outline SOW for Dedicated/Private if we need strict in-territory cold backups.

Yes, Friday 9/3 11:00 PT works for our security lead. Please send calendar invite and a short proposed agenda. Also please include the SOC2 snapshot you attached earlier and the Drive link that maps to the audit schema.

Appreciate it — Olivia
